question: How should seven methodology skills apply the Redis video's orientation with a Valkey/BSD preference and stronger technical evidence?

source_records.evidence_class: primary documented semantics or attributed organizational statement

claims.summary: Valkey is an in-memory data structure store usable for databases, caches, messaging and streams.
Native structures and atomic operations provide alternatives to application-level read-modify-write.
Persistence, asynchronous replication, Sentinel and Cluster are distinct capabilities.

source_records.evidence_class: primary documented semantics or attributed organizational statement

claims.summary: Documented lineage compatibility is Redis OSS 7.2 and earlier, not unrestricted Redis compatibility.
Redis CE 7.4+ persistence files are incompatible; RESP compatibility does not prove backup compatibility.
Client, configuration, scripting and module compatibility require distinguishing old shared APIs from later features.
Server identity can expose compatibility version fields; inventory actual engine identity, not only a Redis-compatible version string.
Migration examples are version-specific and cannot establish target-write rollback safety for every deployment.

source_records.evidence_class: primary documented semantics or attributed organizational statement

claims.summary: RDB snapshots preserve a point in time and expose later writes to loss.
AOF durability and latency depend on fsync policy; everysec has a loss window.
Background persistence forks; fork pauses and copy-on-write memory must be accounted for.
AOF rewriting, truncated logs and backup/restore require integrity and recovery handling, not just enabling a flag.

source_records.evidence_class: primary documented semantics or attributed organizational statement

claims.summary: Default replication is asynchronous; acknowledged writes can be missing on a promoted replica.
WAIT/WAITAOF can reduce risk but do not turn the topology into a strongly consistent CP system.
Partial/full synchronization has different costs and can add recovery load.
Expiry propagation and replica read behavior mean restored/replicated state needs explicit lifecycle checks.

source_records.evidence_class: primary documented semantics or attributed organizational statement

claims.summary: Cluster shards keys using 16,384 slots, with hash tags allowing intentional colocation.
Multi-key commands, transactions and scripts require the relevant same-slot boundary.
Cluster availability has failure/partition limits and does not guarantee strong consistency or zero acknowledged-write loss.
Resharding and client redirects are operational concerns requiring version/topology-aware clients.

source_records.evidence_class: primary documented semantics or attributed organizational statement

claims.summary: MULTI queues commands and EXEC runs them without interleaved client commands.
Queue-time errors differ from execution-time errors; successful earlier/other commands are not rolled back on runtime error.
WATCH supports optimistic check-and-set behavior and requires conflict handling.
Transactions and scripts do not create a transaction across independent stores or external effects.

source_records.evidence_class: primary documented semantics or attributed organizational statement

claims.summary: Server-side scripts reduce round trips and isolate execution from other commands.
Script execution blocks other server work, making bounded computation important.
Scripts should declare accessed keys and parameterize inputs; script cache/loading behavior matters for clients.

source_records.evidence_class: primary documented semantics or attributed organizational statement

claims.summary: Pub/Sub has at-most-once delivery and offline subscribers can miss messages.
Subscriptions do not constitute retained durable work; applications needing eventual effects need another recovery authority.

source_records.evidence_class: primary documented semantics or attributed organizational statement

claims.summary: Streams retain ordered entries with explicit trimming and consumption choices.
Consumer groups expose pending deliveries; XACK marks processing acknowledgement.
Abandoned pending work requires explicit claim/reclaim behavior rather than reading only new messages.
Redelivery and claim races do not establish exactly-once external processing.
Trimming can remove payloads needed by pending consumers, so retention and recovery coverage must be coordinated.

source_records.evidence_class: primary documented semantics or attributed organizational statement

claims.summary: maxmemory eviction accounting excludes replication/AOF buffer memory.
noeviction rejects writes that need more memory; it is not protection from every deletion, expiry or OOM.
Cache eviction and authoritative-record retention have different correctness requirements.
LRU/LFU implementations are approximate; policy choice should follow observed access patterns.

source_records.evidence_class: primary documented semantics or attributed organizational statement

claims.summary: Synchronous loops may primarily measure network and client latency.
Connections, concurrency and realistic pipeline length change what a benchmark measures.
Compare equivalent persistence/fsync requirements when comparing to transactional stores.
Network, dataset, payloads, client limits and workload distribution constrain transferable results.

source_records.evidence_class: primary documented semantics or attributed organizational statement

claims.summary: Redis 7.2 and earlier retain BSD-3-Clause.
Redis 7.4 introduced RSALv2/SSPLv1; Redis 8 added an AGPLv3 option.
An OSI-approved copyleft option is distinct from a permissive BSD license and from governance trust.

source_records.evidence_class: primary documented semantics or attributed organizational statement

claims.summary: Redis added AGPLv3 with Redis 8 in May 2025.
Redis leadership explicitly acknowledges its 2024 relicensing damaged community relations.
The announcement is the vendor's own account, not evidence that all trust concerns disappeared or a neutral performance benchmark.

source_records.source_interest: Project/vendor-hosted account; no independent benchmark or population inference.

source_records.evidence_class: primary documented semantics or attributed organizational statement

claims.summary: The Linux Foundation announced Valkey in March 2024 after Redis relicensing.
Valkey continued from Redis 7.2.4 under BSD-3-Clause with community and corporate participation.
Foundation participation supports the governance-history claim, not a guarantee against every possible future project decision.

source_records.evidence_class: primary documented semantics or attributed organizational statement

claims.summary: Google publishes a broad internal AGPL restriction, demonstrating one organization's policy friction.
Its policy and risk characterization are not universal legal interpretations or a survey of business preferences.

source_records.evidence_class: primary documented semantics or attributed organizational statement

claims.summary: GNU advocates AGPL to preserve access to modified server program source for remote users.
This countervailing rationale demonstrates that copyleft and permissive-license preferences serve different values.
Do not infer that all users agree with either GNU's rationale or Google's policy.

source_records.evidence_class: primary documented semantics or attributed organizational statement

claims.summary: Fedora recorded a Redis-to-Valkey replacement change in response to the earlier source-available relicensing.
It is a named open-source distribution decision from before the AGPL addition, not proof of post-AGPL population sentiment.

source_records.evidence_class: primary documented semantics or attributed organizational statement

claims.summary: Valkey-search provides native vector search as a BSD-licensed module with specific version prerequisites.
Its RediSearch compatibility is explicitly a subset; vector API similarity does not prove every full-text/search feature.
Index attributes, filtering and HNSW tuning require data-dependent recall/latency/memory qualification.
Hash versus JSON indexing and update/delete/recovery lifecycle require feature-specific verification.

source_records.source_interest: Project/vendor-hosted account; no independent benchmark or population inference.

source_records.evidence_class: primary documented semantics or attributed organizational statement

claims.summary: Sorted-set range cost includes result size; bounded top-k avoids implying constant-time unbounded fetches.
Ordering, range mode and returned values are part of application semantics.

source_records.evidence_class: primary documented semantics or attributed organizational statement

claims.summary: HSET field updates are atomic command operations, while complexity scales with the number of fields.
Field operations alone do not prove multi-object invariants.

source_records.evidence_class: primary documented semantics or attributed organizational statement

claims.summary: INCR provides a native single-counter update instead of racing GET/add/SET.
Integer/type constraints must be handled at the application boundary.

claims.summary: Valkey describes its lineage from Redis and the history of BSD commitments followed by relicensing.
Valkey launched under Linux Foundation governance after the 2024 change.
This is project-authored history and should not be treated as a population survey.

The report links Harbor's own issue, PR and release; it supports a named post-AGPL open-source choice, not community-wide preference prevalence.
Its performance and deployment instructions are not incorporated as verified catalog runbooks or benchmark results.

claims.summary: Harbor's March 2026 issue states that repeated Redis licensing changes created risk and proposes Valkey's more friendly license.
The issue also requires smooth migration, so a licensing preference does not waive compatibility work.

source_records.evidence_class: primary project decision record

claims.summary: Harbor's own PR records the cache-backend replacement and links the licensing-risk issue.
The PR was merged on April 28, 2026; this establishes a concrete post-AGPL project decision, not community-wide sentiment or a benchmark.
